## ✨ Key Features

## 💡 What Is Vibe-Trading? Vibe-Trading turns finance questions into research reports, runnable backtests and paper portfolios. You can also authorize a supported broker to execute live trades within a mandate you set and can halt. Your funds stay with the broker. ## ✨ What You Can Do | Task | Where to start | |---|---| | Research markets, filings or uploaded documents | Ask in Web chat or [attach a report](guides/research.md#upload--analyze-documents). | | Backtest a strategy or benchmark alphas | Inspect charts and trades in Run Detail, or compare factors in `/alpha-zoo`. | | Simulate trading or replay a journal | Track daily fills and NAV in `/paper-trading`. Use `/journal` and `/shadow` in the CLI to review your trades. | | Combine accounts or compare allocations | Open `/portfolio` for holdings and proposed allocation changes. [Broker support](#broker-support-at-a-glance) | | Explore options and correlations | Open `/options` for multi-leg payoffs and Greeks, or `/correlation` for market regimes. | | Coordinate or repeat research | Run a [Swarm team](guides/research.md#swarm-workflows), assign work in Pixel Office or schedule a brief in `/scheduled`. | | Revisit research with dated evidence | Search `/research-artifacts`, compare any two revisions, and export a full series or selected comparison as JSON or Markdown. [Versioned research](guides/research.md#versioned-research-artifacts) | ## ⚡ Quick Example Once you have run `vibe-trading init`, you can ask for a backtest in plain English or benchmark an existing alpha library from the terminal. ```bash vibe-trading run -p "Backtest a BTC-USDT 20/50 moving-average crossover for 2024. Compare it with buy-and-hold and report maximum drawdown." vibe-trading alpha bench --zoo gtja191 --universe csi300 --period 2018-2025 --top 20 ``` Open **Run Detail** to compare the crossover with buy-and-hold, inspect the trades behind a drawdown and check the data source on the run card. ### Portfolio drawdown periods In **Run Detail > Portfolio Studio > Risk X-Ray**, inspect the five deepest observed drawdowns, with peak, trough, recovery and duration. A drawdown still open at the end of the input window is reported separately even when it is outside the deepest five. The same `drawdown.episodes` data is saved in `artifacts/risk_xray.json`, summarized in `artifacts/risk_xray.md`, and returned by the `portfolio_risk_xray` Agent/MCP tool. This is a constant-weight return model, not account NAV, strategy P&L or a forecast. Backtests use the average executed basket weights; the model itself does not include fees or cash flows. Duration counts observed bar intervals from peak to recovery, or to the window's end if unrecovered, not calendar days. Daily, weekly and monthly observations retain their original labels. A missing interior return or non-positive/non-finite model wealth makes the periods unavailable, rather than an empty set or zero risk. Values within a relative `1e-12` of a running peak are treated as at that peak to avoid an extra recovery bar caused only by floating-point noise; smaller differences are not distinguished. The JSON report declares this as `recovery_rtol`. Existing scalar statistics and older reports without episode metadata remain supported. ## 🧪 Research Workflow | Step | In the crossover example | |---|---| | Plan | Identify the trading pair, date range, moving averages and benchmark from the prompt. | | Ground | Fetch historical bars for BTC-USDT. Check the source and dates before interpreting the result. | | Execute | Write the strategy and run the backtest. The run directory holds the strategy, trades and equity curve. | | Validate | Compare the result with buy-and-hold. Inspect turnover, drawdown and validation warnings alongside return. | | Revisit | Open the saved run or ask a follow-up with different parameters. You can also save a dated research conclusion and revise it when new evidence arrives. | ## 📡 Data Sources & Smart Fallback The loader supports **28 market-data sources**. With `source: "auto"`, it infers the market from the symbol and tries the configured sources in order. | Market | How a request is filled | |---|---| | A-shares and Hong Kong | Start with Tencent. If it cannot supply the bars, try Eastmoney and then the remaining sources for that market. | | US equities | Start with Yahoo. Stooq and Sina are the next two sources in the chain. | | Crypto | Try OKX, Binance and CCXT before falling back to other sources. | | Futures | Chinese contracts can use AKShare or local bars. Supply local bars for global contracts. | You can also choose a source explicitly. For example, installing `vibe-trading-ai[ashare]` adds the token-free BaoStock loader for daily A-share bars. The [data source reference](guides/capabilities.md#-data-sources--smart-fallback) lists the full chains and credential requirements. ## 🔩 Detailed Capabilities ### Market research | Feature | What you can do | |---|---| | Filings and holdings | Compare a manager’s SEC 13F holdings across quarters, or look through an ETF to its underlying positions. Each holdings report carries its reporting date. | | Company valuation | Use `/dcf` to see how a valuation changes with the discount rate and terminal growth. Use `/comps` for peer multiples, or build a linked three-statement model and export the results to Excel. | | Papers and documents | Search arXiv and OpenAlex for a signal, inspect the authors’ definition, then test it on your own universe. Upload a filing, spreadsheet or slide deck for questions about a specific exhibit. | | Stock screening | With Gildata enabled, screen companies by market cap and retrieve half-year revenue in one request. Screening and portfolio factor diagnosis each have their own opt-in. | ### Quant research | Feature | What you can do | |---|---| | Alpha Zoo | Benchmark signals from Qlib, Alpha101, GTJA and the academic and fundamental libraries. Compare information coefficients across horizons, then check whether the result survives a walk-forward test. | | Backtest engines | Model A-share price limits, crypto funding or futures margin. Use a shared capital pool for a cross-market strategy and inspect the individual fills behind its returns. | | Options Lab | Build a spread leg by leg. Compare its expiry payoff with the Greeks and see how the position responds to a change in spot price and implied volatility. Export the exact analysis request and result as JSON or the full expiry and scenario grid as CSV. The `options_strategy_compare` Agent/MCP tool compares up to four strategies on a shared spot/IV grid with baseline-relative P&L. | | Portfolio risk | Inspect drawdowns, estimate value at risk and expected shortfall, or use Brinson attribution to separate allocation from stock selection. Risk X-Ray reports each holding's signed contribution to portfolio volatility, including hedges that offset risk. The correlation view shows when markets start moving together. | | Strategy tracking | Register a strategy with its evidence and track how its Sharpe ratio or factor information coefficient changes as new results come in. | Risk X-Ray includes `risk_contributions` in the Agent tool response and saved JSON/Markdown reports. Components use `weight × Cov(asset return, portfolio return) / portfolio volatility`, with the same sample and annualization as total volatility. Each `assets` row names its `symbol`; `risk_contribution` is annualized decimal volatility and `contribution_pct` is in percentage points. They add up to total volatility, not portfolio return. A hedge can have a negative risk share, and another holding can exceed 100%; shares are unavailable for zero volatility or an insufficient sample. This is a historical weighted-basket diagnosis, not realized PnL attribution or a forecast. ### Accounts and trading | Feature | What you can do | |---|---| | Portfolio | Bring read-only broker holdings into one snapshot or import an extraETF export. Enter target weights to preview the value change for each holding. | | Paper trading | Advance a saved account one trading day and inspect fills, cash and NAV. You can also replay an A-share session in five-minute steps in a separate simulation. The `paper_trade_reconcile` agent/MCP tool independently checks fees, cash, positions and NAV arithmetic without market or broker access. | | Shadow Account | Import your broker’s trade journal, inspect fees and trading habits, then compare the actual trades with a rule-based replay. | | Broker connections | Set up a connection in the CLI or Web and test it with a read. For supported live profiles, set symbol, order and exposure limits before enabling trading. The kill switch halts live activity. | ### Teams and recurring research | Feature | What you can do | |---|---| | Swarm and Pixel Office | Run a bull–bear investment committee or a quant research desk and inspect the workers’ reports. In Pixel Office, assign a task to a teammate and record the result on the shared board. | | Scheduled briefs | Start from a premarket brief, an earnings tracker or a portfolio checkup. Choose a schedule and send the report to a configured channel such as Slack, Telegram or email. | | Research history | Search older sessions and reopen a saved run. Save a dated conclusion with its evidence and compare revisions when the investment case changes. | | Run records | Inspect the data source, model, execution record and metric references behind a backtest. Reopen the saved trades and equity curve to check a reported figure. | ### Broker support at a glance
Compare read-only, paper and live support by broker **Read** means a dedicated read-only profile. **Sim** means paper orders through a broker sandbox or local simulation. **Live** means live orders under a mandate. Yes indicates a declared capability. ## 🚀 Quick Start **Terminal.** Install the package with Python 3.11+, choose a model provider in the setup wizard, then open the interactive CLI. ```bash pip install vibe-trading-ai vibe-trading init vibe-trading ``` **Web app.** Docker serves the frontend and API together at `http://localhost:8899`. From a fresh checkout, configure your provider before starting the container. ```bash git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/Vibe-Trading.git cd Vibe-Trading cp agent/.env.example agent/.env # Set your provider and API key in agent/.env. docker compose up --build ``` The PyPI package includes the CLI, API and MCP server. For a frontend development setup or a local model, see the [installation guide](guides/installation.md). ## 🖥 CLI Reference Start `vibe-trading` for the interactive terminal. Type `/help` at the prompt to browse commands or use these shortcuts during research. | Command | Use it to | |---|---| | `/model` | Switch the provider or model for the session. | | `/history` | Browse and resume a prior conversation. | | `/show ` | Inspect the results of a saved run. | | `/pine` | Export the current strategy as a Pine Script indicator. | From the shell, `vibe-trading alpha list` browses the factor libraries and `vibe-trading playbook list` shows the scheduled research templates. ## 💡 Examples - **Compare stocks.** Ask “Compare AAPL and MSFT over 2024. Which month accounts for the largest gap in returns?” Resume the conversation later with `/history`. - **Review your trades.** Use `/journal` to analyze your exported trade history, then `/shadow` to compare your trades with a rule-based alternative. - **Run an investment committee.** Choose a stock and follow the bull and bear cases through to the final report. ```bash vibe-trading --swarm-run investment_committee '{"target":"TSLA","market":"US"}' ``` ## 🌐 API Server Start a local server with `vibe-trading serve --port 8899`. In a second terminal, run `curl http://localhost:8899/runs` to list saved runs. Use the returned ID with `GET /runs/{run_id}` to inspect its results. | To run a research session over HTTP | Endpoint | |---|---| | Create the conversation | `POST /sessions` | | Send the research question | `POST /sessions/{id}/messages` | | Follow progress as it happens | `GET /sessions/{id}/events` | Open `http://localhost:8899/docs` to try the endpoints interactively. [Authenticated clients](guides/cli-and-api.md#security-defaults) send the API key in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. ## 🔌 MCP Plugin MCP clients can launch the same package over stdio. Add this entry to Claude Desktop’s `claude_desktop_config.json`, restart the client and call `list_skills`. ```json { "mcpServers": { "vibe-trading": { "command": "vibe-trading-mcp" } } } ``` For other clients or a custom output directory, see the [MCP configurations](guides/mcp.md). ## 🏛 Ecosystem Vibe-Trading is part of the **[HKUDS](https://github.com/HKUDS)** agent ecosystem:
